ops.text: Takes-The-Tools: the King of the Murkmire root cave mouth as its plugin builds it (rockcaveentrance02 round its AutoLoadDoor01, rockcliff08 and rockcliff02 behind), dug into the root layer under the hist, its roots clasping both jambs; facing east to the hiring camp; bones and tools at the threshold. No sign names it. The hiring camp's searchers keep two candles and a totem at the mouth as a warning. Their feet have worn a path back toward the camp.

ops.why: The hill behind the cave mouth. Skyrim's cave-mouth rock is a shell made for a hillside. This site is flat jungle floor, so the open back of the rock (azimuths 192..305, band 38.30..50.50 m) stood free. The hill's flat top stands 0.24 m over the open band along the back face of the mouth and 13 m west of it, then falls to the floor over 10 m and stops short of the tunnel. Vanilla buries the backs of its cave mouths under hillside. King of the Murkmire sets its mouths at the foot of a rise ringed with cliff pieces.
sources: owner walk 11 reply, item 1 (a hillock behind the mouth)

ops.why: The foot of the hill. It wraps both flanks of the cave mouth, so the rock rises out of a slope on three sides. The hill falls to the floor in two easy stages, not one steep drop. It stays at least 13 m from the tunnel and the threshold, so the way in is still level.
sources: owner walk 11 reply, item 1 (a hillock behind the mouth)
tooling/.reports/16k/walk11/places-a/root-hollow-2.md (round 3 reader: hard seam at the north flank, a flat-topped hill)

ops.why: The crown of the hill: a rounded ridge along its long axis, so the hill rises to a crest with no flat top. The mound's 13 m blend gives the crest its round shape.
sources: tooling/.reports/16k/walk11/places-a/root-hollow-2.md (round 3 reader: a flat-topped hill with a squared lip)

ops.why: The north flank of the hill beside the cave rock, as one slope. It holds 47 m up to the rock's north foot, then blends over 10 m into the ground, which lies at 40 to 41 m around x 3684 to 3686. Flat steps with short blends appear as bare terraces between the hill and the rock.
sources: tooling/.reports/16k/walk11/places-a/rh4/rh4g-fill.py (variant V14: no raise in the walkable tunnel; the ground falls from 47 m to 40-41 m over x 3678-3686)
tooling/.reports/16k/walk11/places-a/root-hollow-4g.md (round 1 readers: stepped pale terraces on the north flank)

ops.why: A mound against the back of the cave rock. The rock's north back corner stood 2 to 12 m clear of the ground between x 3670 and 3674, which left a dark slot behind it. The mound raises the ground to meet the rock 1.5 to 2.5 m under its top edge. Inside the shell, west of the door, the ground falls away.
sources: tooling/.reports/16k/walk11/places-a/root-hollow-4b.md (r4b reader: dark slot under the rock's back-left edge)

ops.why: The top step of a fill against the rock's north back corner, at 50.6 m, level with the back mound at 50.5 m. The rock's back edge stands 0.8 to 1.9 m above it.
sources: tooling/.reports/16k/walk11/places-a/rh4/rh4f-fill.py (variant e: ground 49.0 to 50.5 m from z 4552 to 4557 at x 3672-3675, the rock top flush to 2 m under it on the low corner, 0.8 to 1.9 m above it further south; no raise in the tunnel)

ops.why: The middle step of the same fill. It buries the rock's top, which dips at this corner.
sources: tooling/.reports/16k/walk11/places-a/rh4/rh4f-fill.py (variant e: ground 49.0 to 50.5 m from z 4552 to 4557 at x 3672-3675, the rock top flush to 2 m under it on the low corner, 0.8 to 1.9 m above it further south; no raise in the tunnel)

ops.why: The lowest step of the same fill. It joins the slope down the north flank, so the corner has no hollow between the hill and the rock.
sources: tooling/.reports/16k/walk11/places-a/rh4/rh4f-fill.py (variant e: ground 49.0 to 50.5 m from z 4552 to 4557 at x 3672-3675, the rock top flush to 2 m under it on the low corner, 0.8 to 1.9 m above it further south; no raise in the tunnel)

ops.why: The hill's south shoulder, one even slope from the top of the cave rock's back at 50.5 m down to the jungle floor east of the mouth, falling 0.7 m per metre.
The foot of the south shoulder beside the cave mouth's south jamb. It rises 0.4 m per metre southward from the floor of the opening, so the shoulder meets the floor on an easy slope.
The hill's north shoulder, one even slope from 48.8 m beside the cave rock down to the jungle floor east of it, falling 0.7 m per metre.
Fills the corner between the north shoulder and the cave rock's north side, so the ground meets the rock with no hollow between them.
The north side of the mound behind the cave rock, one slope falling 0.6 m per metre from the mound top to the hill foot at 44.5 m, so the mound has no steep north face.

Walk 12: the cave rock's open back rim at its top rear (x 3665 to 3668, z 4563 to 4570) stood 0.6 to 1.5 m over the hill, the gap the owner saw. This mound lifts the hill to the rim's top (51.2 to 52.0 m) along that stretch, so the rock sinks into the hill.

Walk 12: the seat of the canopy giant on the hill top (t-crown-giant). The tree's root plate needs level ground; a 16 m pad at the height of the crest gives it that, wide enough for the full-size tree's root plate. The 10 m blend keeps the crest round.
sources: owner walk 12: a big tree with big roots on the hill top

ops.why: A low apron under the south foot of the hill, from x 3646 to 3680. It holds the ground at 41 m for 6 m before it falls to the jungle floor, so the hill's south side comes down in two stages.

ops.text: Walk 12 owner point: a canopy giant on the hill top, its roots spread over the crest, the roots that hang into the hollow below. The landmark the hollow is found by from the jungle floor. Walk 12 part 4: scale 0.8 and yaw 40, the largest that stands on the hill top without floating (at scale 1.0 its foot floats 3.7 to 10 m at every yaw; at 0.85 by 0.47 m). Four hist roots (r-root-*) run from its foot down the flanks to make it read as rooted in the hill.

ops.text: Walk 12 part 5: four hist roots from the Curse of Cipactli set run down the south-east, north-east, west and north flanks, so the tree reads as rooted in the hill. A fifth root on the south-east flank was dropped because it sank too deep in the slope. Walk 12 part 6: kept clear of the trunk, they read as loose props on the hill, so each now starts at the trunk foot (the pivot end of histroots03 and 02 at the trunk; the south-east root is a histroots03 in place of histroots04, whose centred pivot left only a buried loop 10 m out) and is bound grows-from the tree, the relation that lets a root touch its trunk and its sibling roots.

ops.evidence: plugin: King of the Murkmire 0x8835b10 BlackPlane01 in its cave mouth

ops.text: The tunnel's darkness as King of the Murkmire makes it (BlackPlane01 stood upright inside its rockcaveentrance01 mouth, ref 0x8835b10, rot x -90): here stood upright across our rockcaveentrance02's tunnel 3 m behind the pivot, its foot on the tunnel floor, facing out along the tunnel axis (kit bearing 106, world 96); rays from the lip meet the tunnel's back wall 3.5 m behind the pivot (walk 11). Walk 12: the deep pose sat round the bend, unseen; the card now stands 0.35 m behind the door threshold [3683.5, 4564.2] at scale 0.6, its centre 38.36 m (the lip ground hides the bottom row below 37.6, the roof the top above 40), seen at 56 % from the approach eye with the 1.2 m arrival zone clear (darkCardRule, walkRule, walkwayRule green). Walk 12 part 5: one card at scale 1.5 still left the top-south of the throat lit and showed its corner on the skyline, so it is now one of two cards: this one at scale 1.2 over the lower and middle throat, d-dark-2 over the top-south. Together they cover 92 % of the throat seen from the approach eye, with no card edge outside the rock.

ops.evidence: plugin: King of the Murkmire 0x8835b10 BlackPlane01 in its cave mouth

ops.text: The second darkness card, beside d-dark in the same plane and raised, fills the top-south of the throat that one card could not reach without its corner showing above the rock (walk 12 part 5). The two cards are judged together. Walk 12 part 6: its top-south corner still showed as a black wedge on the upper-left shoulder in the eye render, though the check passed; the check now samples every card's own surface and fails a seen point with no roof of rock over it. Lowered 1.5 m and turned to yaw 100, the wedge is gone and the two cards cover all of the roofed throat.

Low shrubs cover the line where the ground meets the cave rock on both flanks and along its back edge on the hill. Three more stand at the foot of its face north of the mouth. Bracken ferns cover the foot of its face on both sides of the mouth. Bracken ferns grow on the slope south of the mouth. Bracken stands in three clumps on the open hilltop behind the rock. A tree fern stands at the foot of the hill's north slope. Skyrim places ground cover along the same line at its cave mouths. The larger ferns are left out because the flora kit seats them 0.9 to 2.7 m below the ground, most of their height. The King of the Murkmire ring at ref 0x801afd0 uses rockcliff02, dirtcliffsisland01, hist_root05 and hist_vines01 pieces. All four are left out. The cliffs sit too deep in this hill. The banks read as loose slabs on the open floor. The roots stand as open hoops beside the rock on every pose tried on this hill. The vine reads as a bare trunk. A leafy hanging vine crossed the rock's overhang on its south flank and stood 1.4 m off the face beside the opening, so none is placed. The shrub at the rock's north-west back corner now stands 2 m out from it, clear of the rock and its neighbours. The small shrub beside it is gone. The mound m-hill-back-nw meets the rock there, so no cover is needed at that seam.

ops.why: Bones that the beast drags out to its mouth, thickest by the door.
Hoarvor ticks (creature.hoarvor, contents c2) live in the bone scatter at the mouth.
A lost forager's spade, dropped at the mouth: evidence for SX08.
A lost forager's hoe, dropped beside the basket at the mouth: evidence for SX08.
The wamasu that takes the tools (creature.wamasu, contents c1) lies up in the den, among the remains it has dragged there.
One thing worth the fight: a vial of Hist sap beside the bones of the forager who died for it, by the chest at the far end of the hollow under the Hist roots (contents l1).
A lost forager's fishing pole, dropped beside the net at the mouth: evidence for SX08.
The lip of the cave mouth, where the way down into the hollow begins.
Tools dropped in front of the mouth, the evidence for SX08.

ops.text: Walk 12: g-cover-b6, b7 and w3 stood where the giant's roots now spread over the crest; removed, the roots cover that ground.
Walk 12 part 5: g-cover-b1, b5 and f1 stood where the hist roots now run down the flanks; removed, the roots cover that ground and the place stays inside its 88-piece budget.

Walk 12 close-out: histroots02 carries a detached island that lay on the ground about one trunk-width out as a loose shard; swapped to histroots03 (pivot at its end) at yaw 150, so it runs from the trunk foot and leaves no fragment.

ops.why: The north-west back corner of the cave rock: one rim vertex at x 3666.7 z 4552.7 stood 0.55 m over the hill. The ground there is lifted to the rim so no gap shows behind the rock.
Hanging moss on the trees here; a forager cuts it and it grows back. (bmv:landscape/plants/florahangingmoss03aaa, chunk_7_9_vegetation.bin#27:181)
